summary.text: Rich McCormick is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 7th Congressional District. A former Marine Corps helicopter pilot and Navy officer who became an emergency room physician, he was first elected to Congress in 2022 from the 6th District and won the redrawn 7th District in 2024.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, McCormick was raised by a single mother, worked as a paperboy in middle school, and earned a degree from Oregon State University.

He joined the U.S. Marine Corps and became a helicopter pilot; his official biography says he deployed to combat zones in Africa, the Persian Gulf, and Afghanistan during about two decades of service.

He taught at Georgia Tech and Morehouse College as the Marine Officer Instructor, and in the Navy reached the rank of Commander and served as Department Head for Emergency Medicine in Kandahar, Afghanistan.

McCormick earned an M.B.A. from National University and an M.D. from Morehouse School of Medicine, where he was student body president, and completed an emergency medicine residency through Emory, training at Grady Hospital in Atlanta.
He worked as an emergency medicine physician, including with Gwinnett Medical Center and Northside Hospital.
In 2020 he ran for Georgia's 7th District as the Republican nominee and lost to Rep. Carolyn Bourdeaux (D) in the general election.
McCormick won the 2022 Republican primary runoff for the 6th District over Jake Evans (66.5% to 33.5%) and the November 2022 general election over Bob Christian (62.2% to 37.8%).
After redistricting, he won re-election in the 7th District in 2024 over Bob Christian (64.9%), and advanced from the unopposed May 19, 2026 Republican primary.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he was assigned to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (chairing its Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee), the Armed Services Committee, and the Foreign Affairs Committee; his official biography also lists the Oversight Committee.
According to his official biography, he lives in Alpharetta, Georgia.
